name: World Wide Web
hook: The system Tim Berners-Lee built at CERN — six facts cover what Jeopardy keeps asking.

facts.label: Tim Berners-Lee
facts.statement: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989–90 while at CERN; he was knighted in 2004.

facts.label: CERN
facts.statement: CERN, the particle-physics lab near Geneva, released the Web free to all on April 30, 1993, after considering a user fee.

facts.label: the first browser
facts.statement: Time said that "on the seventh day" Berners-Lee cobbled together the Web's first browser, which he wrote himself.

facts.label: blue links
facts.statement: Web links are blue because Berners-Lee made them so; asked why, he answered, "There is no reason."

facts.label: WWW
facts.statement: The three-letter abbreviation WWW was first proposed in 1989 by software developer Tim Berners-Lee.

facts.label: toile d'araignee mondiale
facts.statement: The Academie Francaise officially translates the World Wide Web as "toile d'araignee mondiale" — literally "world spiderweb."

facts.label: Yahoo!
facts.statement: Yahoo! began as "Jerry's Guide to the World Wide Web," created by Jerry Yang and David Filo.
